name: Gateshead

licensing.selective: Selective licensing in 16 neighbourhoods, in two phases: phase 1 (including Bensham, The Avenues, Windmill Hills, Beacon Lough East, Birtley and Chopwell) from 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2030, and phase 2 (more of central Gateshead, Felling and Swalwell) from 1 October 2025 to 30 September 2030.
licensing.additional: Additional HMO licensing for smaller HMOs of three or four unrelated people in the same designated neighbourhoods, from 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2030; larger HMOs need a mandatory licence.
licensing.fee: £850 for a selective licence and £976.30 for an additional HMO licence, with a £75 discount for accredited landlords

housing: Gateshead stretches from the Tyne riverside to the rural Derwent valley. Inner areas such as Bensham, Saltwell and Felling are built up with Tyneside flats (pairs of upstairs and downstairs flats behind separate front doors) and Victorian terraces, where much of the private renting is found, while large post-war council estates surround the town and western areas such as Whickham and Ryton are more suburban. The council has used selective landlord licensing in parts of the inner borough and publishes information about its schemes on its website.
checkinTips: Tyneside flats in Bensham and Saltwell: record which yard, outhouse and bin belong to the flat, and photograph the separate front door, stairs and back lane access.
Victorian terraces in Low Fell and Felling: check for damp at the base of walls and in rear kitchens, and photograph sash or replacement windows.
Back lanes behind terraces: photograph rear gates, yard walls and bins, and note any fly-tipping at the start of the tenancy.
Post-war estate houses: record the boiler, windows and doors, and the condition of gardens and fencing.
Flats in town centre blocks: note fob and key counts, lifts, communal entrances and bin stores.
Homes in the Derwent valley and on hillsides: photograph gutters, steps and retaining walls, and any damp on exposed walls.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Gateshead Council's private sector housing team, which also runs its landlord licensing, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
